title: Benchmark findings — retrieval-quality gap vs. flat-context baseline
description: PH-6 (EPIC-5) built the benchmarking harness itself; this epic is downstream of it — understanding and acting on what the harness actually measured. Run B in project-management/BENCHMARKS.md (llama3.1:8b judge, nomic-embed-text embeddings, n=50, seed=42) shows the SDK's with-SDK retrieval path scoring below a flat-context (no SDK) baseline overall (84.0% vs 94.0%, -10.0%), with the widest gaps on multi_session (-30.0%) and temporal_reasoning (-30.0%), smaller gaps on extraction and knowledge_update (-10.0% each), and a clear SDK win on abstention (+30.0%). BENCHMARKS.md's own Run B analysis already proposes two candidate fixes (larger top_k; wiring the ENH-3/ENH-4 Consolidator/Reconciler hooks so cross-session facts consolidate into a single SemanticFact) — but that analysis is a hypothesis, not yet confirmed against the actual retrieved context for the failing questions. This epic's stories first confirm root cause with real evidence (BENCH-1), then fix what's confirmed, breaking the largest fix (Consolidator/Reconciler wiring into the benchmark's write/search path) into its own sub-stories since it touches the harness's core retrieval loop, not a config tweak. Every story here re-runs the retrieval-quality suite and records the before/after category deltas in BENCHMARKS.md so the fix is measured, not just asserted — same discipline PH-6 itself was built to enforce.
